subject: Renewal planning: capacity acceleration, temporary price hold & credit proposal
messages:
From: Ava Ramos <ava@cedarlabs.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@cedarlabs.com
Date: 2027-04-07T16:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal planning: capacity uplift + short-term rate protection

Soojin / Ben — thanks again for the call this morning. Cedar Labs is preparing our FY28 budget and we expect a meaningful uplift in inference usage starting July (approx +60% month-over-month for 3 months) as we launch a new product line. Two asks from procurement that I wanted to put on the table early: 

1) Can Redwood provide a short-term price hold for the renewal window (we need rate certainty while our legal and budget cycles complete)? Specifically request: a 60-day price hold on current rates from our renewal date.

2) If we commit to a 20% uplift in committed capacity for the next 12 months, we are asking for a one-time bridging credit to offset expected overage in Q3 while usage ramps.

I attached March usage and a brief forecast. Hoping to get a proposal we can show leadership this Friday.

Attachments: [CedarLabs_MonthlyUsage_Mar2027.csv]

Best,
Ava Ramos
Head of Platform
Cedar Labs
ava@cedarlabs.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-07T17:03:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Renewal planning: capacity uplift + short-term rate protection

Looping you both in — summary above from Ava (Cedar Labs). They want a 60-day price hold and a bridging credit if they increase commit by ~20%.

Ben: can we model a bridging credit that covers expected overage in the ramp months (Jul–Sep) and still keep unit economics healthy? If we offer a 60-day rate hold, we should pair it with an agreed true-up and a commit increase (or optional burst pool) to avoid open-ended exposure.

Jordan: procurement/legal will want short amendment language for a limited price hold and clear triggers for credits/true-ups. Can you draft a short amendment template we could push? Aim for a one-page AMM (attachment) and include the rate-hold window, credit calc, and termination clause.

Quick priorities:
- Ben: draft numbers and a couple of option tiers (conservative / balanced / aggressive).
- Jordan: legal sketch for AMM and fallback (if they don’t sign within 60 days, revert to standard rates).
- I’ll propose a timeline to Ava and ask for confirmation on exact uplift cadence.

Thanks — Soojin
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[internal note: share usage forecast with pricing model]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: finance-ops@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-08T10:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: capacity uplift + short-term rate protection

Thanks — ran numbers against their March baseline and Ava’s ramp forecast. Here are three straightforward options we can present (clean bullets for their leadership):

Option A — Conservative (minimal downside protection):
- 20% commit increase for 12 months.
- One-time bridging credit equal to 75% of estimated overage cost for Jul–Sep (calculated from forecast).
- No rate hold beyond the signature date; offer a 30-day courtesy hold while Legal reviews.

Option B — Balanced (preferred):
- 20% commit increase for 12 months with 6-month step-up grace (billing aligned to actual usage).
- One-time bridging credit covering 100% of forecasted overage for Jul–Sep, offset on first two invoices post-renewal.
- 60-day conditional price hold from renewal effective date; hold applies only if AMM signed within 60 days.
- Lock current per-token rate for 12 months thereafter.

Option C — Aggressive (sales-led concession):
- 25% commit for 18 months.
- 100% bridging credit + additional month of credits if they exceed forecast by >20%.
- 90-day price hold.
- 10% off on overage rate for the first 3 months of uplift.

I attached a Draft_AMM_v2_CedarLabs.pdf with language for Option B (balanced). Key assumptions and breakpoints are in the appendix of the draft. From a finance lens, Option B keeps payback and unit economics acceptable while demonstrating partnership.

Attachments: [Draft_AMM_v2_CedarLabs.pdf]

If we go with B, we should require a minimal written confirmation of the uplift cadence (monthly forecast) and an executive sponsor (Ava’s leader) to expedite sign-off.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Ava Ramos <ava@cedarlabs.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@cedarlabs.com, legal@cedarlabs.com
Date: 2027-04-09T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: capacity uplift + short-term rate protection

Soojin / Ben — appreciate the quick turnaround and the three options. After an internal review, Cedar Labs prefers Option B (Balanced). A few clarifications before I send to finance/legal for execution: 

- We’ll confirm the 20% commit increase in writing by April 20 (monthly cadence attached to forecast).
- The 60-day conditional price hold is acceptable provided the AMM language has a clear reversion clause if signatures lapse.
- For the bridging credit, please include an example calculation in the final AMM showing how the Jul–Sep credit is computed and how it applies to invoice offsets.

Please send a redline-friendly AMM and I’ll route through procurement/legal. If we can get that by end of day tomorrow, I’ll push finance to prioritize the signatures.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this finalized quickly.

Best,
Ava Ramos
Head of Platform
Cedar Labs
